Integration gives $\int_{\gamma_i}e_j=2\pi i\delta_{ij}$, so the comparison is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf. Let $\tau_{\le a}$ denote the canonical truncation, with degree $a$ equal to the kernel of the next differential. Since every degree-$k$ logarithmic form has at most $k$ poles, the identity gives a genuine chain inclusion $\tau_{\le a}L\to W_aL$. By step 2.2 it induces an isomorphism in degrees at most $a$ and both sides have no cohomology above $a$, hence is a quasi-isomorphism for every $a$. These inclusions commute with the maps as $a$ increases. We therefore have the filtered comparison zigzag $(Rj_*\mathbb Q_U\otimes\mathbb C,\tau)\to(Rj_*\mathbb C_U,\tau)\leftarrow(L,\tau)\to(L,W)$, all arrows graded quasi-isomorphisms; exact scalar extension and the local finite torus cohomology establish the first arrow. (Actual filtered global-section models and a single comparison.) The sheaf comparison in step 3.1 is a zigzag, so it must not be treated as a nonexistent direct sheaf map in the opposite direction. Resolve the complexes and their filtrations by the exact Godement construction: $C^0(A)(V)=\prod_{x\in V}A_x$, with the natural embedding and successive cokernels. Stalks and products are exact for vector spaces under AC. Moreover $C^0(A)=\prod_{x\in X}i_{x*}A_x$ is an injective sheaf of field-vector spaces: each $A_x$ is injective over its field by extension of linear maps along a chosen complement, the exact stalk functor is left adjoint to $i_{x*}$, and a product of injectives is injective because the component extension maps can be chosen simultaneously under AC. The successive cokernel construction therefore gives an actual injective resolution. Exactness of $C^0$ and the short exact augmentation sequences give exactness of each successive cokernel functor by the snake lemma, so the resulting functorial resolution is exact on filtration levels, their finite intersections and both associated gradings; its global-section total computes derived global sections. Apply it to $L$ with $W,F$ and to the other weight-filtered models in the zigzag. Replace the rational and comparison models by $\tau_{\le d}$ first; their cohomology sheaves above $d$ vanish by the local torus calculation, so this is a quasi-isomorphism and leaves a finite weight range $0\le a\le d$. After resolution and global sections the complex-coefficient arrows in the zigzag are maps of weight-filtered vector-space complexes with graded quasi-isomorphisms. For the rational scalar-extension arrow, the global graded comparison is the isomorphism $H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)\otimes\mathbb C\to H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb C)$ from [F3], with the normalization of step 3.1; this proves it is a graded quasi-isomorphism without interchanging tensor product with an infinite product of stalks. Such a map admits a weight-filtered homotopy inverse: its cone has acyclic weight-graded complexes; a cycle in $W_a$ has a leading graded preimage, and subtracting its differential lowers the cycle to $W_{a-1}$, so finite induction supplies a preimage in $W_a$. Thus the cone is acyclic with a $W$-strict differential. Choose filtration-compatible complements of its cycles and right inverses of its differential; the resulting degree-minus-one homotopy contracts the cone and preserves $W$, and the cone homotopy equations give a $W$-filtered homotopy inverse of the original map. AC permits these linear complements. Inverting the leftward comparison in step 3.1 and composing the remaining arrows gives an actual $W$-filtered chain map $K_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C\to K_{\mathbb C}$, with $K_{\mathbb C}=\Gamma(X,C^\bullet(L))$ carrying the original $W,F$. Its graded maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Different inverse choices are filtered-homotopic, so their induced comparison and image filtrations on cohomology agree. These are bounded-below degreewise-finite filtered models of the type required in [F5].

(Strictness on the weight-graded global models.) Exactness of the resolution and step 2.1 identify $\operatorname{Gr}^W_aK_{\mathbb C}$ with a global-section resolution of $\Omega_{D^{[a]}}^\bullet[-a]$, with its degree Hodge filtration shifted by $a$. Its Hodge spectral sequence degenerates at $E_1$ by [F3]. This implies strictness of the differential of this actual filtered vector-space complex: if $dx$ belongs to $F^p$, take the leading $F$ index $b<p$ of $x$; its class in the associated-graded complex is a cycle. Degeneration means this $E_1$ class lifts to an actual cycle $y\in F^b$, up to an element of $F^{b+1}$ and a boundary in $F^b$. Subtract that cycle and boundary from $x$, preserving $dx$ and raising the filtration index of the preimage. Repeat through the finite filtration until a preimage of $dx$ lies in $F^p$. Thus $\operatorname{im}d\cap F^p=d(F^p)$. Moreover its degree-$r$ cohomology is $H^{r-a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)$ under the comparison of step 3.1, with the induced $F$, pure of weight $r-a+2a=r+a$ and finite-dimensional by [F3]. Hence the global comparison models of step 4.1 satisfy every graded axiom of a rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex, including strictness and the full induced Hodge filtration.

(The mixed structure and its spectral sequence.) Apply the full conclusion of [F5] to the proved mixed Hodge complex of step 5.1. Its cohomology is $H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$ by steps 3.1-5.1 and [F6], and it carries the image Hodge filtration and shifted weight filtration $W_mH^n(U)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(W_{m-n}K)\to H^n(K))$. The weight spectral sequence is $E_1^{-a,q}=H^{q-2a}(D^{[a]};\mathbb Q)(-a)$, pure of weight $q$, degenerates at $E_2$, and gives $\operatorname{Gr}^W_mH^n(U)\cong E_2^{n-m,m}$ with its induced Hodge filtration. In particular this step uses the supplied recurrent-to-image-filtration proof, not an assumption that higher differentials preserve the desired filtration.

(Lower weight bound and compactification image.) The pole index $a$ is nonnegative, so a term contributing to total degree $n=q-a$ has weight $q=n+a\ge n$. Hence step 6.1 gives $W_{n-1}H^n(U)=0$. Also $W_nH^n(U)$ is the image of $H^n(W_0K)$. On the complex side $W_0L=\Omega_X^\bullet$ by step 1.2; on the rational side $\tau_{\le0}Rj_*\mathbb Q_U=\mathbb Q_X$, since a punctured-coordinate polydisc is connected. Its map to $Rj_*\mathbb Q_U$ is restriction. Thus both sides identify $W_nH^n(U)$ with the actual image of $j^*:H^n(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^n(U;\mathbb Q)$, compatibly with the rational comparison and Hodge filtration.

(Functoriality and independence.) A compactified extension $f:(X,D)\to(Y,E)$ of an open morphism satisfies $f^{-1}(E)\subseteq D$. Locally a target boundary equation pulls back to a unit times a product of source boundary equations with nonnegative integer exponents, so $f^*d\log t=d\log u+\sum_i m_i d\log z_i$. Wedges preserve pole count and degree, hence $f^*$ preserves $W,F$ on the logarithmic complexes and is compatible with the rational meridian comparison. The functorial resolutions and filtered comparison homotopies of step 4.1 produce the same natural pullback on cohomology; [F5] therefore makes it a mixed Hodge morphism. The graph-extension construction in [F7] supplies such compactified extensions after modifying the source. For two SNC compactifications of one $U$, a common SNC domination gives pullback comparison maps between their logarithmic mixed Hodge structures on $H^n(U)$, whose underlying rational maps are the identity. Strictness in [F5] makes these identity maps isomorphisms for both filtrations, proving independence. For any smooth projective compactification with arbitrary boundary, the modification-image clause of [F7] identifies its restriction image with the SNC one, so the formula of step 7.1 holds for it too.

(Choice and boundary cases.) AC is inherited through the typed suppliers in [A1] and is also used exactly in step 4.1 for exact products in the Godement resolution and filtration-compatible vector-space complements to strictify the comparison zigzag. The monomial contractions, residues, rational meridian normalization, finite filtrations and weight bookkeeping are otherwise choice-free. With empty boundary $L=\Omega_X^\bullet$ and $W_0=L$, recovering the pure projective structure; empty $U$ may be represented by empty compactification and has zero cohomology, while the SNC compactification hypotheses already require density on every nonempty component. Components of differing dimensions are handled separately, empty strata vanish, and degrees outside the cohomological range give zero groups. This completes the retained full mixed Hodge, functoriality, independence, lower-weight and image claims.

Assume AC. For every field $k$, every space $X$, and $n\ge0$, evaluation gives a natural $k$-linear isomorphism
$$H^n(X;k)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_k(H_n(X;k),k).$$
There is no finite-dimensional hypothesis. The right side is the full algebraic dual.

Assume AC. Let $U$ be smooth quasiprojective over $\mathbb C$, and choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, boundary $D$. The logarithmic de Rham complex with Hodge filtration by degree and pole-count weight filtration constructs a functorial rational mixed Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$, independent of the compactification. Its weights are at least $n$, and
$$W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow H^n(U,\mathbb Q)).$$

A **rational mixed Hodge structure** consists of a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $H$
with a finite basis ([[def-linear-basis]]) together with

- a finite increasing filtration $W$ of $H$, the **weight filtration**, and
- a finite decreasing filtration $F$ of
  $H_{\mathbb C}:=H\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$, the **Hodge filtration**
  ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),

such that the following opposition condition holds on every weight-graded
piece. Here a filtration is **finite** when $W_aH=0$ for all sufficiently
negative $a$ and $W_aH=H$ for all sufficiently positive $a$, and dually
$F^aH_{\mathbb C}=H_{\mathbb C}$ for $a\ll0$ and $F^aH_{\mathbb C}=0$ for
$a\gg0$ ([[def-increasing-and-decreasing-filtration-of-an-object]]).

**Conjugation.** The $\mathbb{Q}$-linear involution $\sigma$ of
$H_{\mathbb C}$, defined on generators by
$\sigma(h\otimes z)=h\otimes\bar z$ and extended $\mathbb{Q}$-linearly,
satisfies $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$ and $\sigma(cz)=\bar c\,\sigma(z)$ for
$c\in\mathbb C$ ([[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]). It preserves the
subspace $W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=(W_aH)\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$ for every $a$,
so it descends to each graded piece
$\operatorname{Gr}^W_aH_{\mathbb C}:=W_aH_{\mathbb C}/W_{a-1}H_{\mathbb C}$
([[def-associated-graded-object-of-a-filtered-object]]). The **conjugate
Hodge filtration** is $\bar F^q:=\sigma(F^q)$, a finite decreasing filtration
of $H_{\mathbb C}$.

**Opposition.** Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-vector space with
finite decreasing filtrations $F$ and $\bar F$, and let $n$ be an integer. The
two filtrations are **$n$-opposed** when the natural map
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}\bigl(F^pV\cap\bar F^qV\bigr)\longrightarrow V,\qquad (v_{p,q})_{p+q=n}\longmapsto\sum_{p+q=n}v_{p,q},$$
is an isomorphism. Applied to $V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ this
condition is required for every $n$, with the *induced* filtrations: $F^p$
acts on $\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$ through the image of
$F^p\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$, and $\bar F^q$ through the image of
$\bar F^q\cap W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. Writing
$$H^{p,q}_n:=F^p\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}\cap \bar F^q\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C},$$
the requirement is therefore the direct sum decomposition
$$\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}_n \qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb Z .$$
Since $\sigma$ interchanges the induced filtrations $F^p$ and $\bar F^p$ and
preserves $W$, it maps $H^{p,q}_n$ onto $H^{q,p}_n$, so
$\overline{H^{p,q}_n}=H^{q,p}_n$. Equivalently, the opposition condition requires both
$F^pV\cap\bar F^qV=0$ whenever $p+q>n$ and
$F^pV+\bar F^{n+1-p}V=V$ for every $p$, on
$V=\operatorname{Gr}^W_nH_{\mathbb C}$. The conjunction, rather than either
condition alone, is equivalent to the displayed decomposition: the spanning
condition and the modular law give
$F^pV=F^{p+1}V+(F^pV\cap\bar F^{n-p}V)$, and the vanishing condition makes
this sum direct; descending induction through the finite filtration gives
$F^pV=\bigoplus_{a\ge p}(F^aV\cap\bar F^{n-a}V)$ and then the decomposition
of $V$. Conversely, the decomposition gives these two conditions by grouping
its summands by the first and second indices.

**Morphisms.** A morphism $f\colon H\to K$ of rational mixed Hodge structures
is a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear map with $f(W_aH)\subseteq W_aK$ for all $a$ and
$f_{\mathbb C}(F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq F^pK_{\mathbb C}$ for all $p$, where
$f_{\mathbb C}=f\otimes\mathrm{id}$. Such an $f$ commutes with the
conjugations $\sigma$, hence also satisfies
$f_{\mathbb C}(\bar F^pH_{\mathbb C})\subseteq\bar F^pK_{\mathbb C}$.

**Substructures, pure structures, Tate.** A subspace $H'\subseteq H$ with the
induced filtrations $W_aH'=H'\cap W_aH$ and
$F^pH'_{\mathbb C}=H'_{\mathbb C}\cap F^pH_{\mathbb C}$ is a **substructure**
when the induced filtrations again satisfy the opposition condition on every
graded piece, and a quotient $H\to Q$ with the quotient filtrations is a
**quotient structure** under the same requirement; that the kernel, image and
cokernel of a morphism do carry such structures is not part of the definition
and is proved in the strictness lemma below. A structure is **pure of weight
$n$** when $W_{n-1}H=0$ and $W_nH=H$; the opposition condition then says that
$H_{\mathbb C}=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^{p,q}$ with
$H^{p,q}=F^p\cap\bar F^q$, and $\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$. The **Tate
structure** $\mathbb Q(r)$, for $r\in\mathbb Z$, is the pure structure of
weight $-2r$ with $\mathbb Q(r)_{\mathbb C}=\mathbb C$ concentrated in type
$(-r,-r)$, that is $H^{-r,-r}=\mathbb C$ and $H^{p,q}=0$ for
$(p,q)\ne(-r,-r)$.

**Tensor and dual conventions.** The tensor product $H\otimes K$ carries
$$W_a(H\otimes K)=\sum_{b+c=a}W_bH\otimes W_cK,\qquad F^p(H\otimes K)_{\mathbb C}=\sum_{b+c=p}F^bH_{\mathbb C}\otimes F^cK_{\mathbb C},$$
where the sums of subspaces are those of the complexifications, and the dual
$H^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H,\mathbb Q)$ carries
$$W_aH^*=\{u:u(W_{-a-1}H)=0\},\qquad F^pH^*_{\mathbb C}=\{u:u(F^{1-p}H_{\mathbb C})=0\}.$$

**Polarizability.** A pure rational Hodge structure $H$ of weight $n$ is
**polarizable** when it carries a rational bilinear form $Q$ of parity
$(-1)^n$ that pairs only complementary Hodge types, i.e.
$Q(H^{p,q},H^{p',q'})=0$ unless $p'=n-p$ and $q'=n-q$, and whose
Weil-operator Hermitian form $h(u,v):=Q(Cu,\bar v)$, where the Weil operator
$C$ acts as $i^{p-q}$ on $H^{p,q}$, is positive definite.

No mixed structure in this definition is assumed to split over $\mathbb R$ or
over $\mathbb Q$; the Deligne splitting constructed below is a decomposition
over $\mathbb C$ only.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The $a=0$ column has $E_1^{0,0}=\mathbb Q(0)$, $E_1^{0,1}=0$, $E_1^{0,2}=H^2(\mathbb P^1;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q(-1)$, pure of weight $2$ and type $(1,1)$; the $a=1$ column has $E_1^{-1,2}=\mathbb Q(-1)^2$ and is otherwise zero. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every projective morphism in the finite-dimensional
H-projective convention of this page is proper: if $f:X\to S$ factors over $S$
as
$$X\xrightarrow{i}\mathbb P^n_S\longrightarrow S$$
with $n\ge0$, $i$ a closed immersion and the second arrow the projection, then
$f$ is proper. The empty source, the empty base and the case $n=0$ are
included, and no Noetherian, field, reducedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is
imposed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
Jacobian-criterion, ample-powers, Chern-form and comparison suppliers below.
Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex scheme of pure dimension $n\ge0$.

Then the closed points of $X$ carry a structure of **complex manifold**
$X^{\mathrm{an}}$, its **analytification**: if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $n\ge1$
this is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth complex manifold of complex
dimension $n$
([[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]); if $n=0$ it is the
finite discrete set $X(\mathbb C)$ with its unique complex structure in the
convention of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]]; and if
$X=\varnothing$ then $X^{\mathrm{an}}=\varnothing$. Every standard smooth
algebraic chart of $X$ becomes a holomorphic chart of $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, and
every morphism of smooth complex schemes $X\to Y$ induces a holomorphic map
$X^{\mathrm{an}}\to Y^{\mathrm{an}}$.

Moreover, for every ample invertible sheaf $A$ on $X$ there is a smooth
positive closed real $(1,1)$-form $\eta_A$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ whose de Rham
class is the real image of the topological first Chern class
$c_1(A):=c_1(A^{\mathrm{an}})\in H^2(X^{\mathrm{an}};\mathbb Z)$:
$$J_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}[\eta_A]=\rho_{X^{\mathrm{an}}}\bigl(c_1(A)\bigr),$$
where $J$ is the de Rham comparison and $\rho$ the change of coefficients
$\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R$
([[lem-rational-cohomology-scalar-comparison-for-compact-smooth-manifolds]]).
In dimension $n=0$ and for $X=\varnothing$ every $2$-form and every degree-two
cohomology class is zero and $\eta_A=0$, so the identity holds trivially.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism locally of
finite presentation ([[def-locally-finite-presentation-morphism]]) and let
$x\in X$ with $s=f(x)$. Then $f$ is smooth at $x$
([[def-smooth-morphism-schemes]]) if and only if there are affine open
neighbourhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$ and
$V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $s$ with $f(U)\subseteq V$ and a presentation of
$C_h$, for some $h\in C\smallsetminus\mathfrak q$ with $\mathfrak q$ the prime
of $x$, as
$$C_h\;\cong\;\Bigl(A[t_1,\dots,t_m]/(f_1,\dots,f_r)\Bigr)_g,$$
in which some $r\times r$ minor of the Jacobian matrix
$\bigl(\partial f_j/\partial t_i\bigr)$ has image a unit of $C_h$. Such a chart
is flat over $A$ with geometrically regular fibres whose components have
dimension $m-r$; in the local-dimension convention of
[[def-relative-dimension-smooth-morphism]] it exhibits relative dimension
$m-r$ at $x$.

The criterion demands that *some* presentation have an invertible $r\times r$
minor; it does not demand this of an arbitrary redundant equation list, and
$r>m$ makes an invertible $r\times r$ minor impossible by definition of the
matrix shape.

Let $m,n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^m\times\mathbb C^n$ be open, let
$f:U\to\mathbb C^n$ be holomorphic, and let $(a,b)\in U$ satisfy $f(a,b)=0$.
Assume the complex Jacobian with respect to the second block is invertible:

$$\det\left(\frac{\partial f_j}{\partial w_k}(a,b)\right)_{1\le j,k\le n}\ne0.$$

Then there are neighbourhoods $A$ of $a$ and $B$ of $b$, and a unique
holomorphic map $\varphi:A\to B$, such that

$$f(z,\varphi(z))=0\qquad(z\in A),$$

and, after shrinking $A\times B$ if needed,

$$f(z,w)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad w=\varphi(z).$$

Let $D\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ be open and let
$F:D\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth. For every base point $(t_0,x_0)\in D$ there are
$h>0$ and an open neighbourhood $W$ of $(t_0,x_0)$ such that each initial pair
$(s,y)\in W$ has a unique solution on $[s-h,s+h]$, and the resulting local
solution map is smooth in the initial time and initial state.

Let $F(t,x,\lambda)$ be jointly $C^\infty$ in $(t,x,\lambda)$ on an open time-state-parameter
domain. Near any base data $(t_0,x_0,\lambda_0)$ there are a compact time
interval $I$ and a neighbourhood $W$ of $(x_0,\lambda_0)$ such that, for every
$(y,\lambda)\in W$, the solution of

$$x'(t)=F(t,x(t),\lambda),\qquad x(t_0)=y,$$

is defined on $I$, and the resulting solution map is smooth in the pair
$(y,\lambda)$.

Let $V:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be a smooth vector field on an open set $U$, and for
each $x_0\in U$ let $x(\,\cdot\,;x_0)$ denote the unique maximal solution of
$x'=V(x)$ with $x(0)=x_0$. Then the maximal solution domain

$$\Omega:=\{(t,x_0)\in\mathbb R\times U:t\text{ lies in the maximal interval of }x(\,\cdot\,;x_0)\}$$

is open in $\mathbb R\times U$. On $\Omega$, the evaluation map
$\Phi(t,x_0):=x(t;x_0)$ is smooth in the state variable and continuous jointly in
$(t,x_0)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a closed smooth
manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Then $M$ has the homotopy type of a finite
CW complex ([[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $X$ be a metric space
([[def-metric-space]]) having a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets at
every point, and let $k$ be a field. Write $k_X$ for its constant sheaf. There
are natural isomorphisms
$$H^q(X,k_X)\cong H^q_{\operatorname{sing}}(X;k)$$
in every degree, where the left side is derived cohomology in the category of
sheaves of $k$-vector spaces (computed with the functorial $k$-linear injective
resolutions supplied by
[[lem-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]]; compare
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]). The same assertion holds on
every open subset of $X$. In particular a nonempty contractible space with this
local property has constant-sheaf cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero
otherwise. This applies to every finite-polyhedral open star and to its
nonempty intersection with a closed simplex.

Assume AC and the actual geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of the Verdier theorem. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved constructible subcategory, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_k C^*(F;k)$, with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models below; proper maps already satisfy it. Their finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.

Assume AC. For a compact Kähler manifold $X$ in the sense of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], every de
Rham class has a unique smooth harmonic representative and
$$H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X),\qquad \overline{H^{p,q}(X)}=H^{q,p}(X).$$
Here $H^{p,q}(X)$ is precisely the set of classes with a $d$-closed smooth
representative of type $(p,q)$, so the decomposition is independent of the
Kähler metric. Writing $\Omega_X^p$ for the sheaf of holomorphic $p$-forms (the
kernel of $\bar\partial$ on the sheaf $\mathcal A^{p,0}$ of smooth $(p,0)$-forms),
$H^{p,q}(X)$ is isomorphic to $H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$, the sheaf cohomology of
[[def-sheaf-cohomology-derived-global-sections]]. The Hodge filtration
$F^a=\bigoplus_{p\ge a}H^{p,k-p}$ of $H^k(X;\mathbb C)$ equals the filtration
induced by the holomorphic-degree filtration of the de Rham complex, whose
spectral sequence has $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X,\Omega_X^p)$ and degenerates at $E_1$.
Pullback by holomorphic maps of compact Kähler manifolds and cup product
preserve Hodge type, so $H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ is a functorial rational pure Hodge
structure.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), inherited from the
analytic suppliers below. Let $X$ be a compact Kähler $n$-fold in the
conventions of
[[def-compact-kahler-manifold-and-hodge-polarization-conventions]], with
Kähler form $\omega$, and let $0\le k\le n$. On the primitive space $P^k$ put
$$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k},$$
where $a,b$ are closed smooth representatives of the classes and the integral
is independent of the representatives. This form is $(-1)^k$-symmetric, pairs
$P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, and for nonzero $a\in P^{p,q}$ satisfies
$$i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)=(n-k)!\,\|a_{\mathrm{harm}}\|_{L^2}^2>0.$$
If $[\omega]=\ell\in H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$, then $Q_k$ is a rational polarization
of $P^k$, and full $H^k$ is polarized by the orthogonal direct sum form $S_k$
that on $L^rP^{k-2r}$ is $(-1)^rQ_k$, equivalently
$S_k(L^ru,L^rv)=Q_{k-2r}(u,v)$ for $u,v\in P^{k-2r}$; degrees $k>n$ are
polarized by transporting the polarization of $H^{2n-k}$ along $L^{k-n}$, with
Tate shift. For every real Kähler class the same positivity and nondegeneracy
statements hold, without rationality. In particular this applies to smooth
closed complex projective submanifolds of projective space with a hyperplane
polarization, hence to smooth projective complex varieties through their smooth
projective analytifications; more generally it applies to every real Kähler
class, including $\ell+\epsilon\eta$ when represented by a positive closed
form. For any continuous family of Kähler classes the primitive kernels (of
every fixed degree $0\le k\le n$) vary continuously as subspaces; rational
primitive spaces are asserted only at rational classes.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a smooth partition of unity subordinate to it.

Assume AC. Let $R$ be a commutative PID and $X,Y$ spaces such that every $H_q(Y;R)$ is a finite free $R$-module. For every $n\ge0$ the additive singular cohomology cross product gives an isomorphism
$$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(X;R)\otimes_RH^q(Y;R)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^n(X\times Y;R).$$
All indices are nonnegative. The symmetric assertion holds when every $H_p(X;R)$ is finite free instead. No bound on the number of nonzero homology degrees and no finite-rank hypothesis on the singular chain groups is required.

Fix a commutative unital ring $R$. A **left $R$-module local system** on a
space $X$ is a covariant functor
$$\mathcal L:\Pi_1(X)\longrightarrow R\text{-}\mathbf{Mod},$$
where the source is [[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]], functor means
[[def-functor-and-contravariant-functor]], and the target is the category in
[[prop-modules-and-homomorphisms-form-category-rmod]]. Write
$\mathcal L_x$ for its value at $x$ and
$$T_\gamma=\mathcal L([\gamma]):\mathcal L_x\longrightarrow\mathcal L_y$$
for transport along a path $\gamma:x\to y$. Every arrow of the source has a
reversed inverse, so functoriality makes every $T_\gamma$ an isomorphism, with
$T_{\bar\gamma}=T_\gamma^{-1}$ and
$T_{\alpha*\beta}=T_\beta T_\alpha$.

A **morphism of local systems** $\eta:\mathcal L\to\mathcal K$ is a natural
transformation ([[def-natural-transformation]]): it is a family of
$R$-linear maps $\eta_x:\mathcal L_x\to\mathcal K_x$ satisfying
$$\eta_yT^\mathcal L_\gamma=T^\mathcal K_\gamma\eta_x$$
for every path $\gamma:x\to y$. Isomorphisms of local systems are natural
isomorphisms.

A continuous map $f:X\to Y$ induces a functor
$\Pi_1(f):\Pi_1(X)\to\Pi_1(Y)$ by $x\mapsto f(x)$ and
$[\gamma]\mapsto[f\gamma]$. Postcomposition preserves constants, reversals,
and concatenation, so this is well defined. The **pullback local system** is
$$f^*\mathcal K=\mathcal K\circ\Pi_1(f),\qquad (f^*\mathcal K)_x=\mathcal K_{f(x)},\qquad T^{f^*\mathcal K}_\gamma=T^\mathcal K_{f\gamma}.$$
Pullback of a coefficient morphism is defined componentwise. Thus
$(gf)^*=f^*g^*$ and $1_X^*$ are literal equalities of functors with these
conventions.

All definitions work independently on every path component. The empty space
has the unique empty local system. No basepoint, universal cover, common fiber,
or choice principle is required.

For later comparison with group rings, if $x$ is fixed and
$g=[\alpha]\in\pi_1(X,x)$, the base fiber is given the **left monodromy
convention**
$$g\cdot m:=T_{\bar\alpha}(m).$$
The reversal is essential: covariance and first-path-first multiplication give
$T_{\alpha*\beta}=T_\beta T_\alpha$, so
$T_{\overline{\alpha*\beta}}=T_{\bar\alpha}T_{\bar\beta}$, exactly the left
action law $(gh)m=g(hm)$.

derivations.claim: Local product structure. The analytification $f^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a proper holomorphic map, because $f$ is projective by hypothesis and projective morphisms are proper by [F1]; its fibres are closed complex submanifolds, compact by properness. At every point of $X$ the smooth algebraic morphism $f$ admits the presentation of [F2], and the holomorphic implicit function theorem of [F2] exhibits holomorphic charts in which $f^{\mathrm{an}}$ is the linear projection of a product of polydiscs; consequently each fibre is a compact complex manifold. In particular, for every $s\in S$ the fibre $f^{-1}(s)$ is compact and, by [F1] applied fibrewise, carries a Kähler structure.

Transport and the cohomology local systems. Choose a smooth horizontal complement to $\ker df^{\mathrm{an}}$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ (locally the product charts of step 1.1 provide one; glue the local choices with a smooth partition of unity on the manifold $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ [F9]). For a path $\gamma:[0,1]\to S$ and a point $x\in f^{-1}(\gamma(0))$, the horizontal ODE $\dot x(t)\in H_{x(t)}$ with $f(x(t))=\gamma(t)$ has a unique maximal solution by [F3]; because $f$ is proper, the lifted solution stays in the compact set $f^{-1}(K)$ for a compact neighbourhood $K$ of $\gamma([0,1])$, so by the openness of the maximal solution domain in [F3] it exists on all of $[0,1]$. The resulting transport map $\tau_\gamma:f^{-1}(\gamma(0))\to f^{-1}(\gamma(1))$ is a diffeomorphism, smooth in the initial point by the smooth dependence on initial data in [F3], and an endpoint-fixed smooth homotopy of paths gives a homotopy of terminal diffeomorphisms by the parameter dependence in [F3]. The terminal point maps need not be identical, but their induced maps on cohomology are identical by homotopy invariance. Piecewise smooth representatives and homotopies suffice for the fundamental groupoid: subdividing a path or homotopy into finitely many parameter pieces lying in coordinate charts and using linear interpolation in smaller convex charts gives the usual piecewise smooth representatives without changing the endpoint-fixed homotopy class. Concatenation and reversal give composition and inverses of the cohomology transports. The assignments $x\mapsto H^m(f^{-1}(x);R)$ for $R=\mathbb Z,\mathbb Q$, together with the isomorphisms $\tau_\gamma^*$, therefore define functors on the fundamental groupoid of $S$, that is, $R$-module local systems in the sense of [F8]; this is the local system $R^mf^{\mathrm{an}}_*\underline R$ of the family.

Identification with the sheaves and integral lattices. On each fibre, and on each product chart of step 1.1, the space is a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, so [F4] identifies singular cohomology with constant-sheaf cohomology there. The proper base change clause of [F5] identifies the sheaf $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with the fibrewise cohomology of the local system of step 2.1; the same identification for $\mathbb Z$-coefficients gives the local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Z$. Each fibre is a closed smooth manifold, so its integral cohomology is finitely generated by [F4]; hence the quotient of $H^m(f^{-1}(x);\mathbb Z)$ by its torsion group is a full finitely generated free lattice in $H^m(f^{-1}(x);\mathbb Q)$, and the transport isomorphisms of step 2.1 preserve the torsion subgroups and these lattices. Passing to the quotient by torsion therefore produces the full monodromy-stable integral lattice of the variation.

Continuous pure Hodge decomposition. Fix $s\in S$ and a smooth trivialization $B\times F\cong f^{-1}(B)$ near $s$ obtained by transporting the whole compact fibre along radial paths in a sufficiently small convex base chart using step 2.1, with $F$ the fibre over $s$. The restrictions of a smooth family of Kähler metrics — for instance the pullback along the projective embedding of the positive closed forms supplied in [F1] — give a smooth family $\Delta_t$, $t\in B$, of formally self-adjoint elliptic Laplacians on the fixed compact manifold $F$, with continuously varying uniformly elliptic coefficients on the fixed manifold; here the smooth family of metrics is obtained from the projective embedding into $S\times\mathbb P^N$ by restricting the Fubini-Study form, and the identification of the fibres with $F$ is the product chart. By the elliptic parametrix and Fredholm theory of [F6], the kernel of $\Delta_{t_0}$ is finite dimensional and the resolvent is bounded from $L^2$ to $H^2$; a fixed contour around $0$ separating the zero spectrum gives, for $t$ near $t_0$, convergent Neumann series for $(\Delta_t-\lambda)^{-1}$ and hence a continuously varying finite-rank projection onto the kernel of $\Delta_t$, compare [F6]. Its rank equals $\dim\ker\Delta_{t_0}$ for $t$ near $t_0$ and the kernel dimension is the constant Betti number of the fixed fibre by [F6], so no nonzero eigenspace can occur inside this contour projection; the projection is smoothing and therefore projects exactly onto the harmonic space; applying the same continuously varying projections to the type projections of the forms yields continuously varying subspaces $H^{p,q}_t$ of the harmonic representatives. Since the decomposition is independent of the metric and functorial by [F6], the resulting family of decompositions of $H^m(f^{-1}(t);\mathbb C)$ is a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of weight $m$ of the local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ in the sense of the definition.

Flat Lefschetz operators and polarization. Let $L$ be a relatively ample line bundle on $X$. Its first Chern class lies in $H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$. Apply the positive Chern-metric construction of [F1] to the ample restriction on each compact fibre, extend that metric to a neighbourhood using the smooth trivialization of step 2.1, and shrink the base chart so vertical positivity persists by compactness. Relative to a fixed smooth reference metric on $L$, patch the logarithms of the local metric ratios with a smooth partition of unity pulled back from the base. On a fibre these base weights are constant, so the resulting Chern curvature is their positive convex combination; it is globally closed, represents $c_1(L)$ and restricts on every fibre to a Kähler form with rational class. No positivity in base directions is asserted. Then in the product chart the restrictions to the fibres induce one and the same class on the fixed model $F$ under the identifications $\tau_\gamma$ of step 2.1, because those identifications are induced by the homotopic family of inclusions of the fibres into $X$ and cohomology is homotopy invariant; explicitly, if $\psi_t:F\to f^{-1}(t)$ are the product-chart identifications, then the maps $(t,x)\mapsto\psi_t(x)$ exhibit the composites $i_t\circ\psi_t$ as homotopic to $i_s\circ\psi_s$, so $\psi_t^*(c_1(L)|_{f^{-1}(t)})=\psi_s^*(c_1(L)|_{f^{-1}(s)})$. Cup product and integration are compatible with the transport isomorphisms, so the map $a\mapsto c_1(L)\smile a$ is a flat Lefschetz operator, and the polarized Lefschetz decomposition supplied by [F7] is flat. The forms $Q_k$ of [F7] applied to the primitive pieces give a flat rational bilinear form, since their defining integrals involve only cup products, the flat powers of the Kähler class just described, and the constant sign $\epsilon(k)$; the positivity clause of [F7] holds on every fibre, and the full polarization is the sign-adjusted orthogonal sum along the flat Lefschetz decomposition, hence also flat, rational and positive. This supplies the flat rational polarization required in the definition.

Geometric closures and full lattices. All assertions are made over a fixed open piece of the base, and may be pulled back along a base change to any smooth $S'$ by change of the parameter. Products: for smooth projective $f_i:X_i\to S$, $i=1,2$, the product family $X_1\times_SX_2\to S$ is smooth projective, and the cohomological Künneth isomorphism of [F8] identifies $R^{m}(f_1\times_Sf_2)_*\mathbb Q$ with the direct sum of tensor products $R^pf_{1*}\mathbb Q\otimes R^{q}f_{2*}\mathbb Q$, $p+q=m$, compatible with Hodge type because pullback and wedge of $(p,q)$ forms preserve bidegree by [F6]; this rational comparison uses [F8] over the field $\mathbb Q$, where the finite-dimensional homology groups are free. The ambient product-family cohomology has a full stable integral lattice by step 3.1; intersecting it with each rational tensor summand gives a full monodromy-stable lattice in that summand, since a rational basis can be multiplied by common denominators into the ambient lattice. Thus products and their full lattices are geometric without assuming that the integral cohomology of every smooth projective fibre is torsion-free. Direct sums are realized by disjoint unions of families over $S$. The degree-two cohomology of the constant family $\mathbb P^1\times S\to S$ is $\mathbb Q(-1)$, of type $(1,1)$, and its rational Hodge dual is $\mathbb Q(1)$, of type $(-1,-1)$, by the dual and Tate conventions in the definition. For a realization $H|_U\subseteq\bigoplus_i R^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i)$, twisting by any integer $r$ gives the realization inside $\bigoplus_i R^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i+r)$, which is allowed directly by that definition; the same rational idempotent remains flat and preserves the shifted Hodge types. Thus all integer Tate twists have the stated geometric realizations, without identifying a positive twist with untwisted degree-two cohomology. For a pure variation of weight $w$, its flat rational nondegenerate polarization of step 4.1 gives $H^*\cong H(w)$ as Hodge variations, so the just-proved Tate realization also realizes the dual; the dual of a full stable lattice is again full and stable. Finite sums of pure weights are handled componentwise. Exterior powers are Hodge direct summands of tensor powers cut out by the rational alternating idempotent, which is flat and a Hodge morphism on every fibre; more generally a prescribed flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism on every fibre cuts out a geometric Hodge direct summand of a realized variation. Intersecting such a rational direct summand with the full ambient lattice of step 3.1 gives its full monodromy-stable lattice: a rational basis of the summand can be cleared to integral vectors of the ambient lattice, and flatness of the summand makes the intersection monodromy-stable. Finally, for a morphism $g:X'\to X$ of smooth projective complex varieties, $g^*:H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X';\mathbb Q)$ preserves Hodge types by the pullback functoriality clause of [F6], so rational pullbacks between smooth projective fibres are morphisms of pure Hodge structures. This proves every closure and lattice clause of the statement concerning a single smooth projective family; the Gauss-Manin family itself is geometric and polarizable by steps 2.1-5.1.

Conclusion. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 produce the finite-rank rational and integral local systems with full monodromy-stable lattices, step 3.2 the continuous pure Hodge decomposition, step 4.1 the flat Lefschetz operators and the flat rational polarization, and step 5.1 the remaining closure, lattice and pullback clauses. Hence $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation in the sense of the definition, with the stated additional properties. No analytic-variation theorem or Gauss-Manin semisimplicity theorem is imported; the argument is the fibre-bundle, harmonic and Künneth construction of the family categories.
